history.summary: CSV NAME FLAG: this row's temple is the famous Shri Haribaldev Jew Temple of Baripada, known as Dwitiya Srikshetra (Second Abode of Lord Jagannath). Built by Maharaja Baidyanath Bhanj of Mayurbhanj in 1575 — legend says he was denied entry to Puri's Jagannath temple in royal dress, camped at Atharnala, and was instructed in a dream to build a Jagannath temple at Baripada 'no grander than the one in Puri'. Built of laterite stone on Puri's architectural principles (84'6" high, with a boundary wall replicating Puri's). The Baripada Rath Yatra, observed since 1575 and the second most popular in Odisha after Puri, is celebrated the day after Puri's festival and is unique: Subhadra's 12-wheeled chariot (Devadalana/Vijaya) is pulled only by women — a tradition begun in 1975 during International Women's Year at the initiative of District Collector Vivekananda Patnaik. name: Jagannath Temple
town_description: Baripada is the district headquarters town of Mayurbhanj district in northern Odisha, set at the foothills of the Simlipal range. A historic princely capital of the Bhanja dynasty, it is Odisha's second most important chariot-festival town after Puri, known as Dwitiya Srikshetra.

travel.road: In Baripada town on the Badadanda; the 3,000-ft procession road runs from the temple to the Mausibadi (Mausi temple)
